specification_anchor_refs.verbatim: 6. Authorization is deny-by-default and evaluated on every executable backend boundary. Hiding UI rows is a projection behavior, never the security boundary.

- root, system, namespace-owner, database-owner, and other privileged SurrealDB sessions MUST NOT execute ordinary protected-resource flows or count as privacy/isolation proof because privileged users bypass table permissions;

State found at ab618f46 (read this before coding): the durable half EXISTS at the storage layer but only as root. SurrealDatabase implements list_debug_breakpoints / set_debug_breakpoints (storage/surreal/database.rs:1476-1495 -> storage/surreal/state_store.rs:680 and :706) against table knowledge_debug_breakpoints (schema.surql:4796-4812, PERMISSIONS NONE); only the Database trait DEFAULT bodies return NotImplemented (storage/mod.rs:2522-2539), and the api/debug_adapter.rs module doc (lines 5-10) is stale when it says the durable half fails closed. The routes (get_breakpoints :277, put_breakpoints :294 @ab618f46) are unauthenticated and run as root; the write's receipt is a KnowledgeRichDocumentSaved event with the constant actor 'debug-breakpoints-ui' (state_store.rs:720-734). First prove the current behaviour with a live-store route test (owner PUT then GET returns the set, not NotImplemented) and record the observation; if the live route does return NotImplemented, the implementation goes through SurrealDatabase as described here.

Authorization: both routes require an authenticated account session and authorize_request(RichDocument, rich_document_id, Read, 'fs.read') for GET and (RichDocument, rich_document_id, Update, 'fs.write') for PUT, and the PUT body's workspace_id must equal the rich document's workspace (already asserted in the transaction: THROW 'HSK-DEBUG-BREAKPOINT-DOCUMENT-WORKSPACE'). Storage calls run inside with_record_user_scope.

Database layer: knowledge_debug_breakpoints gets per-operation predicates: select WHERE fn::mt120_document_access(record::id(rich_document_id), record::id(workspace_id), 'read', 'fs.read'); create and delete WHERE fn::mt120_document_access(..., 'update', 'fs.write') (PUT is replace-all = delete + create); update NONE unless used; plus the owner workspace-delete path keeps working (the table is already covered by REFERENCE ON DELETE CASCADE on rich_document_id/workspace_id - F4 - and by fn::mt120_workspace_delete's zero-row check; make sure an owner with breakpoints can still delete the workspace).

Receipt: the PUT's kernel_event_ledger receipt is accepted by a receipt predicate branch (resource rich_document, action update, fs.write, $session = $auth.id) and carries the session principal as actor instead of the constant 'debug-breakpoints-ui'. The owner can read it via GET /kernel/events/aggregates/debug_breakpoints/:rich_document_id; another account reads 0.

Persistence/reload: breakpoints written by PUT survive closing and reopening the embedded store (same data directory) and are returned by GET after reopen, in (source_url, line) order, with condition and verified preserved; a second PUT replaces the set (no leftovers); uniqueness (rich_document_id, source_url, line) still enforced.

Negatives: anonymous GET/PUT -> constant denial and no rows written; another account's GET returns the constant denial (never the owner's breakpoints) and its PUT leaves the owner's set unchanged (re-read as owner, F3); a same-account read-only principal can GET but its PUT is denied and changes nothing. No regression: storage::surreal::mt136_database_surface_proof_a::mt136_database_surface_proof_a (its loom_navigation case exercises list/set_debug_breakpoints at mt136_database_surface_proof_a.rs:867-940) stays green, and api::debug_adapter lifecycle tests stay green. The api/debug_adapter.rs module doc is corrected.

engine_facts: SurrealDB is pinned =3.2.0 (src/backend/handshake_core/Cargo.toml). Facts verified in surrealdb-core-3.2.0 source by the authority matrix:

F1 Table and field permissions are OFF inside a PERMISSIONS predicate (dbs/options.rs:201 new_for_permission_predicate; doc/check.rs:457-470; exec/permission.rs:87-99). Predicates and the fn::* functions they call see every row and field, including fields that are FOR select NONE.

F2 A top-level query issued on a record-user connection DOES enforce field permissions. Never probe a predicate by running `RETURN fn::...` directly as the record user; it reads permission-hidden fields as NONE and lies. Probe inside a predicate instead (e.g. a probe table whose PERMISSIONS FOR select calls the function).

F3 A denied CREATE, UPDATE or DELETE is SILENTLY IGNORED: no row returned, no error (doc/check.rs:457,469 IgnoreError::Ignore). Every record-user write MUST check the returned row (or a follow-up SELECT) and map an empty result to the constant denial; the failure otherwise surfaces later as a field ASSERT 500, an empty 404, or a guard THROW 403.

F4 REFERENCE ON DELETE CASCADE/UNSET and DEFINE EVENT bodies run with permissions OFF (doc/purge.rs:376,385; doc/event.rs:52,80). Cascades are never blocked by the caller's delete permission, and cascade targets need no delete predicate for the cascade itself.

F5 Session selection: `SurrealStorage::with_record_user_scope(scope, fut)` (src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/surreal.rs:956 @ab618f46) sets a tokio task-local; `with_data_operation` then signs a cloned client in as the record user. Anything outside that scope, INCLUDING work moved into `tokio::spawn`, runs as root. Re-enter the scope inside every spawned future that touches protected tables.
authority_toolkit: Rust authorization entry points (all @ab618f46, src/backend/handshake_core/src/): `api::authority::authorize_request(state, headers, capability_id, ResourceKind, external_resource_id, ResourceAction)` (api/authority.rs:1216) returns an AuthorizedResourceContext whose `.record_user_scope` MUST then wrap the storage call via `state.surreal.with_record_user_scope(ctx.record_user_scope, fut)`. A route that calls authorize_request but writes outside that scope is still ROOT-WRITE.

`api::authority::require_authenticated_session` (api/authority.rs:1013) is the axum route_layer middleware C2 used for process-starting routes with no protected-resource row (see api/debug_adapter.rs:183-186 route_layer). `authenticated_session_credentials` (api/authority.rs:1031) returns the LocalSessionContext + token + channel binding hash. risks: Replace-all PUT under record-user scope: a denied DELETE plus an allowed CREATE (or vice versa) leaves duplicates or a partial set (F3).
The constant 'debug-breakpoints-ui' actor makes the owner's receipt unreadable under the record-user aggregate route (C2 risk pattern).
Workspace delete may become blocked by breakpoint rows if the guard's zero-row check is kept while the cascade is not reached.
Making MT-136's proof pass by running it as root would hide a regression of the record-user path.
minimum_controls: Every positive proof runs as an authenticated record user (account session + channel binding). A root/admin session (with_admin_operation, test_admin_query*, SurrealStorage without with_record_user_scope) may only SEED preconditions that the product itself cannot create, and never counts as privacy/isolation proof (02:2773, LM-RLS-002).

Every changed route has: anonymous negative (no session headers), cross-account negative (a second OwnerSession cannot read or write the first account's rows, and the rows are unchanged afterwards), and where a write is involved, a read-only (viewer) negative when the grant model can express one.
Denied writes are proven by re-reading the canonical row after the call (F3: denied writes are silent). A 403 status alone is not proof that nothing was written.

Anti-scaffold: no new abstraction, trait, feature flag, config knob or helper that is not called by product code in this MT; no `#[ignore]`, no `return Ok(())` skip paths, no assertion weakened or deleted to go green; tests may not assert only on mocks/fixtures the Coder authored for a resource-boundary claim (CODER-PROOF-004, CODER-CODE-006).

No fixture-only proof: each acceptance item is proven against the real embedded SurrealDB store (fresh Handshake-managed RocksDB/SurrealKV directory under the owner runtime root), through the real axum router, with the real ResourceBroker.

Every test binary run must report a NONZERO executed count for the named tests (`running N tests` with N equal to the number of names passed with --exact); a `0 passed` result is a failure of the check, not a pass.
The reopen test uses a fresh process-local store handle on the same data directory; an in-memory cache cannot satisfy it.
